overall: The AG found the Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not naming the nonunion personnel in the notice or announcement and by voting in executive session to extend a contract; no intent found, compliance ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the November 21 meeting failed to identify the nonunion personnel to be discussed in executive session under Purpose 2.
Complaint alleged the chair's pre-executive-session announcement did not identify the nonunion personnel subject to the Purpose 2 negotiations.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, unless disclosure will defeat the purpose for the executive session, the public body should identify the specific personnel that is the subject of the negotiation both in the announcement prior to convening in executive session and on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board finalized an agreement with nonunion personnel by voting in executive session to extend the Police Chief's contract.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by voting in executive session to extend the Chief’s contract.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the violations were intentional; the AG considered whether an intentional violation under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c) was shown.
allegations.key_passage: We have not previously warned the Board against the violations found here, nor do we find other evidence that would support a finding of an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Board argued the complaint should not be reviewed because no copy was filed with the Town Clerk as required by 940 CMR 29.05(3).
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was timely filed with the Board and the Board had the opportunity to review and respond to the allegations raised in the complaint, we review the complaint despite the fact that a copy was not also filed with the Town Clerk.

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged that the Interim Town Administrator and the current Town Administrator violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law applies only to public bodies and individuals acting as public body members; therefore, we decline to review any allegations that the Interim Town Administrator and current Town Administrator violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
